points.reason: The frontend instance produces the instruction-bus request, so its address can be observed, altered, or withheld at the direct output connection.
The LSU instance produces the data-bus request, so its address and read/write direction can be observed, redirected, reversed, or suppressed at the direct output connection.
The register-file instance stores the architectural values, exposes operands on rs1, rs2, and rs3, accepts rf_wdata for writes, and is clocked and reset through lines 319-320.
Register operands enter the ALU through rs1-rs3, and the ALU result contributes to rf_wdata, allowing operand observation or corruption of a register writeback.
The control instance receives rs1 and produces CSR and return-address values that enter rf_wdata, so it can observe an operand or affect a register writeback.
rs2 supplies LSU write data that can reach the data-bus request, while LSU read data and wait status can corrupt or block subsequent register updates.

points.reason: rf_wdata is the write value supplied to the register file, so changing it corrupts architectural contents and withholding it prevents required updates.
The ALU result enters rf_wdata and can therefore corrupt the execution value written to the register file.
The LSU read result enters rf_wdata and can corrupt a load value written to the register file.
Control-produced CSR and return-address values enter the writeback combination and can corrupt architectural results.
rf_wdata combines the execution, load, CSR, and return-address values before supplying the register-file write port.
The PMP instance receives CSR control and data used to change its configuration and produces both configuration readback and permission faults.
xcsr_res only combines PMP readback with other CSR values and does not itself modify or block the PMP configuration.
The control instance generates the CSR write controls and data that the PMP instance receives, allowing configuration modification that can permit or deny accesses.
This writeback combination only carries selected CSR readback and does not change or block the PMP configuration.
The PMP instance produces pmp_fault, so changing the result can permit a forbidden access or fault a valid one.
The disabled-PMP generate branch forces pmp_fault low, removing the protection decision in that build.
The control instance consumes pmp_fault to determine fault handling, so changing it can bypass protection or block a valid access.
The LSU consumes pmp_fault in the memory-access path, so changing it can permit an invalid access or prevent a valid transfer.
The LSU produces lsu_wait, and an asserted or held wait indication can prevent completion of a data access.
Control consumes lsu_wait to determine whether the data access can complete, so a held wait can stall CPU progress.
The LSU produces lsu_err from the data-access path, so it can be changed to suppress a real error or inject one for a valid transfer.
Control uses lsu_err for fault handling, so changing it can misclassify an access and alter or stop execution.
The ALU computes alu_cmp from execution operands and supplies it to control, so changing it can select the wrong branch or an unintended control-flow loop.
Control consumes alu_cmp to choose conditional execution and can be redirected or prevented from completing by a changed comparison result.
irq_machine combines the three machine interrupt inputs, so changing or holding any input changes the request delivered to control.
The control instance consumes irq_machine to enter interrupt handling, so injected or suppressed requests can redirect or starve execution.
firq_i is wired directly to the control instance's fast-interrupt input, so it can be injected, suppressed, or held to redirect execution.
dbi_i is wired directly to the control instance's debug-request input, so asserting it can alter or halt normal execution.
The ALU CSR result enters the CSR readback combination and can corrupt values observed by software.
The counters instance supplies xcsr_cnt to the CSR readback combination, so its result can be corrupted before writeback.
The disabled-counter branch forces xcsr_cnt to zero, changing the CSR value returned for counter reads.
The PMP instance supplies xcsr_pmp to the CSR readback combination, so its returned status or configuration value can be corrupted.
The disabled-PMP branch forces xcsr_pmp to zero and therefore changes the corresponding CSR readback.
The ICC instance supplies xcsr_icc to the CSR readback combination, so its returned value can be corrupted.
The disabled-ICC branch forces xcsr_icc to zero and changes the corresponding CSR readback.
